This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f89d29e382e7d50cfe1b2a98742ac1c3d436cd26` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aeedf724114461043e103fac43bcb4f24439ea43` — the merge of head `0f452e832bc477f7991713d0d21b4a0b91d4a434` into base `f89d29e382e7d50cfe1b2a98742ac1c3d436cd26`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aeedf724114461043e103fac43bcb4f24439ea43 && git checkout aeedf724114461043e103fac43bcb4f24439ea43
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f89d29e382e7d50cfe1b2a98742ac1c3d436cd26 0f452e832bc477f7991713d0d21b4a0b91d4a434 && git checkout -B drift-repro f89d29e382e7d50cfe1b2a98742ac1c3d436cd26 && git merge --no-ff 0f452e832bc477f7991713d0d21b4a0b91d4a434

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f89d29e382e7d50cfe1b2a98742ac1c3d436cd26
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f89d29e382e7d50cfe1b2a98742ac1c3d436cd26` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## REWORK · patch round 1 · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH` · 2026-10-19T21:33Z · head `bf00bb57c`

- **`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/restored-approval-continuation.test.ts`:** two assertions pin the system arm's old shape, which this PR moves. They are the `parked()` helper's `runAs:'system'` expectation, `{ userId: 'submitter', permissions: [], isSystem: true }`, and the post-decision expectation of the `runAs:'system'` approve/reject `it.each`, `{ userId: 'u1', permissions: [], isSystem: true }`. Both now expect `{ userId, isSystem: true }` with no `permissions` key. ⛔ Nothing else in `plugin-approvals` changes.
- **Why the claim's exclusion no longer applies:** it held `plugin-approvals` for #24519 (seat 2), and #24519 has landed. No open PR touches this file (a file scan of the open PRs at this record). This is a test assertion that this PR's change makes false: the #24243 / #24388 precedent, applied to a pin.

After the edit, run `plugin-approvals`' suite (the dev measured 2 failed / 1118 passed on these two cases) and the derived list again on the new head (`--ran`: 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN). The seat then runs the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record on that head, since the change is declared a narrowing.

Every cited file was read at this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The system arm's envelope — right.** `resolveRunDataContext`'s `runAs:'system'` arm now spreads `positions: []` / `permissions: []` only when `context.userId` is absent. A named-user run hands ObjectQL `{ isSystem: true, actor, userId, tenantId?, flowRunId? }`; a user-less run (a schedule) keeps today's envelope byte for byte. The `isSystem`, `actor`, `userId` and `tenantId` lines of the arm are untouched by the diff. Pinned by key absence, not `toEqual` alone (`crud-runas.test.ts`, three cases: the named user, the named user whose trigger forwarded arrays, the user-less control).

2. **No reader of a system context's arrays loses authority — right, traced.** The security middleware's `isSystem` bypass (`security-plugin.ts` `if (opCtx.context?.isSystem) return next()`) is the first statement after the write-epoch bump, which reads no arrays; `getReadFilter` answers `undefined` on `isSystem`; the three capability evaluators short-circuit on `isSystem` before reading. Every other array read in the plugin spells `?? []` or `Array.isArray` (`isPrincipalLessContext`, the CRUD gate, every `collectRLSPolicies` caller, `resolvePermissionSets`, the explain engine), so absent reads as `[]`; `stageRlsMembership` runs only on the de-elevated hook context, after the seed filled it. ObjectQL's `buildSession` now yields `session.positions` undefined where it yielded `[]` on such a write: `HookContextSchema.session.positions` is optional, and both readers guard (`body-runner.ts` `Array.isArray`; `comment-access-hooks.ts` `callerContext` prefers the operation's own system context and hands `positions` to helpers that `?? []`). `ScopedContext.roles` likewise answers undefined; nothing reads `.roles` off an api. `runUserOf` guards with `Array.isArray`, so the flow's `current_user.positions` is `[]` as before; `seedRunGrants` skips `runAs:'system'`; `stampSystemInsertOwner` reads only `isSystem`; the runtime door forwards arrays only when non-empty. The one reader whose answer changes is the one meant to: `ScopedContext[SEED_USER_GRANTS]`'s `needsGrants = !Array.isArray(ctx.permissions)`.

3. **The `runAs:'user'` hook resolves the user's own grants — right, and the narrowing is real.** `withRunAs('user')` copies the write context with `isSystem: false`; the seed finds no `permissions` and resolves the named user's positions, sets and peers through `resolveUserAuthzGrants` in the run's `tenantId`, the resolver the request path uses. Wider for a user holding a set the baseline does not grant (the hook now reads an object it was refused on); narrower where a held set's row policy now applies to the hook's read, which the baseline never applied. Both directions are pinned on the real stack against the user's own request as the oracle, with a GUARD that the two users differ from the baseline in opposite directions and a hand-fired baseline control. The concrete grant detail stays in the seat copy, as ruling `5323310017` requires; this record keeps the same discipline. Two edges, read and judged right: (a) a named-user system run whose trigger carried no `tenantId` (the record-change door forwards `session.organizationId` only when present, the runtime door `ec.tenantId` only when present) resolves the user's organisation-less envelope. `grantAppliesInTenant` admits only global grant rows there, there is no "every organization" mode, and Layer 0 resolves an organisation-less principal's tenant-scoped reads to nothing under `group`, so the hook can read at most what that user's own organisation-less request reads. The card's sentence names "a user and its organisation"; the claim's exclusion names "only when a user is named"; the diff follows the claim, and neither reading leaks beyond the user's own envelope, so this stands as a note for the seat, not a defect. (b) A forwarded ADR-0090 agent ceiling was never honoured on this arm (the old envelope replaced it with `[]`); the record-change door forwards no arrays at all; the delegated hook path is outside this card.

4. **The approvals decider path after ruling `6267719791` Q1 A — right.** `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` deletes the trigger user's positions, permissions, peers and email, sets `userId` to the decider and returns before `seedRunGrants` on a system run; the arm then hands the post-decision writes exactly Q1 A's `{ isSystem: true, userId: the decider }`, no permission resolution for the run, elevation unchanged. The hook a post-decision write fires resolves the decider's grants, and the submit write's hook the submitter's (the `hgp_review` pin). The `engine.ts` docblock that leaned on "a system run's data context carries none" is rewritten to say what the hook now resolves. The approvals status mirror already writes `{ isSystem: true, userId, tenantId? }` with no arrays (PR #24634, merged), so the two producers of the family now obey one rule.

5. **plugin-approvals — right, and nothing else moved there.** Exactly the two expectations the rework record `6277856952` allowed, the `parked()` helper's `runAs:'system'` one and the post-decision one of the `runAs:'system'` approve/reject `it.each`, now read `{ userId, isSystem: true }` with no `permissions` key: one file, +2 −2, the package's only path in the diff.

6. **The published type — right, and declared.** `RunIdentityContext.positions` / `permissions` become optional; `RunDataContext` is that type; both are exported from the package entry. A reader-side narrowing of a published type of `@objectstack/service-automation` (published, `18.0.0-next.5`), named in the changeset with the consequence for a reader; `TypeScript Type Check` is green, so no in-repo reader relied on the required shape.

7. **Unchanged, as excluded by the claim — right.** The `runAs:'user'` arm's code is not in any hunk (the optionality lands on the shared interface, not on that arm); the user-less control keeps `positions: []` / `permissions: []` with no `userId`, and the hook it fires is still refused `HOOK_UNSCOPED_DATA_ACCESS` 403 (pinned); hooks declaring `runAs:'system'` or `'inherit'` are untouched.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/24614-system-run-user-grants.md` matches what the diff publishes: `@objectstack/service-automation: minor`; a `!` title; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the reader's fixed spelling; the `BREAKING` banner, "shipped as minor under the launch-window convention for breaking changes", the form 29 sibling changesets at this head carry; the adr-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker with its why, closing the other categories on facts; and the one-line fix for an author ("declare the hook `runAs:'system'`"). The PR body carries the same `Clause-②` line verbatim from the claim. `no` rather than `yes` is the truthful value: no export, key, option or field is added, two members may now be absent, and the type change is the written form of that shrink. plugin-approvals' change is test-only and owes no changeset. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (the adr-0087 and no-major gates) are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev round 0 (`6277772125`), `deviations`: (1) the plugin-approvals breach not taken — answered by the rework record and landed in round 1 exactly as allowed; (2) grant detail kept off GitHub — consistent with `5323310017`, the public fixture is synthetic; (3) the above-baseline ablation red came from its envelope assertion — acceptable, the below-baseline and decider pins went red on their read assertions, so the behaviour was ablated, not only the shape; (4) the full suite ran before the `7c7741dcb` merge — superseded, round 1 re-ran service-automation in full on this head and `Test Core` 1–6 is green; (5) cli, client and connector tests not run locally — `Test Core` covers them; (6) the body's `Clause-②` line verbatim — matches the changeset. `open_questions: []`.
- Dev round 1 (`6278565512`), `deviations`: the 1132 vs 1120 count (two mirror files now load), the re-run of the full suite, the labeler's labels (`documentation` is the labeler's reading of the changeset path; no doc is edited and none is owed: the docs describe `runAs:'system'` as elevated with the decider as attribution user, which stays true, and the drift check listed release-owned pages only), and the body's single session-URL footer — all in order. `open_questions: []`.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (both rounds): the hook seed resolves no `email`, so an email-keyed row policy in the user's own sets fails closed in such a hook until #24639 lands. #24639 is claimed (`6278068776`, `domain:engine`, file-disjoint). The seat's ordering note `6277888374` states the window correctly in direction and consequence: the RLS compiler puts an unresolved `current_user.email` on the `deniedBy` path, the policy fails closed, nothing leaks, and the window opens when this PR lands and closes with #24639. One imprecision, answered here: "to no rows" holds when that policy is the only one admitting rows of the object; where the user's sets admit rows by other policies, those rows still come. Not escalated.
- Claim exclusions hold on the file list: no `packages/objectql/**`, no `packages/core/**`, the `runAs:'user'` arm untouched, plugin-approvals held to the two assertions. Serial order held: PR #24636 (`14ccb1da9`), PR #24527 (`1b4078077`) and PR #24634 for #24519 (`b61353ffa`) merged before this head. No governed surface in the diff (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); 435 changed lines; the PR is draft with auto-merge off.
- Carried to the seat as a note, not a flag: the organisation-less edge in ① item 3(a). Tightening the arm to a named user with a `tenantId` would keep such a hook on the organisation-less baseline instead; both readings stay inside the user's own envelope, so the choice is the seat's, in a follow-up if at all.
